The clause is not confined to deaths in the course of duty, and the table it carries applies from the lowest band of less than one year of qualifying service.

Exam-safe point: Suicide: the ordinary death gratuity table applies.

Statutory Authority: Rule 45(2), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Assuming the table is limited to natural or duty deaths

q: A son eligible for a share of gratuity is charged with abetting his father's murder. His claim:
opts: remains suspended until the criminal proceedings conclude
is forfeited immediately on the charge being framed
is unaffected, because a charge is not a conviction
passes to his own children in the meantime
expl:
( A) remains suspended until the criminal proceedings conclude.
(B) is forfeited immediately on the charge being framed. — Suspension of the claim is the consequence; forfeiture follows conviction.
(C) is unaffected, because a charge is not a conviction. — Rule 48(1) suspends the claim on the charge itself.
(D) passes to his own children in the meantime. — The rule does not provide for transmission on a charge.

Rule 48(1) suspends the claim of a person charged with murdering the Government servant, or abetting it, until the criminal proceedings conclude. Under rule 48(2) conviction debars him and the share passes to the other eligible members of the family, while acquittal makes the share payable to him. Rule 48(3) applies the same scheme where the death occurs after retirement, and the Explanation includes abetting a death by suicide.

Exam-safe point: Charge suspends; conviction debars; acquittal restores.

Statutory Authority: Rule 48, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Treating the charge as immediate forfeiture

q: Both husband and wife are Government servants and both die. Their eligible child draws two family pensions. Where both pensions are at the ordinary rate under rule 50(2)(a)(i), the combined amount is limited to:
opts: ₹1,25,000 per mensem
₹1,00,000 per mensem
No limit, because two separate pensions are involved
₹75,000 per mensem
expl:
( D) ₹75,000 per mensem.
(A) ₹1,25,000 per mensem. — That ceiling applies where either pension is at the enhanced rate.
(B) ₹1,00,000 per mensem. — That figure does not appear in rule 50(13).
(C) No limit, because two separate pensions are involved. — Rule 50(13) caps the sum precisely because two pensions are involved.

Rule 50(13) deals with the case where both spouses were Government servants. If the surviving child is eligible to draw two pensions at the enhanced rate, or where one enhanced pension later converts to the ordinary rate, the sum is limited to ₹1,25,000 a month. Where both pensions are payable at the ordinary rate under rule 50(2)(a)(i), the sum is limited to ₹75,000 a month.

Exam-safe point: Two ordinary-rate family pensions: ₹75,000 combined.

Statutory Authority: Rule 50(13), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Applying the ₹1,25,000 ceiling to two ordinary-rate pensions

q: Where family pension is admissible to the parents, it is payable:
opts: to whichever parent the Head of Office considers dependent
to the father first, and failing him to the mother
to the mother first, and failing her to the father
to both in equal shares
expl:
( C) to the mother first, and failing her to the father.
(A) to whichever parent the Head of Office considers dependent. — Dependence is a precondition; the order between the parents is fixed by the rule.
(B) to the father first, and failing him to the mother. — Rule 50(10)(b) reverses the usual order and names the mother first.
(D) to both in equal shares. — The rule provides a sequence, not equal shares.

Rule 50(10)(a) makes family pension payable to the parents for life where no widow, widower or eligible child survives, if the parents were dependent on the servant immediately before death. Clause (b) then fixes the order: the mother first, failing which the father. The Explanation deems parents dependent where their combined income is less than the minimum family pension and the dearness relief admissible on it.

Exam-safe point: Parents: mother first, then father.

Statutory Authority: Rule 50(10) and its Explanation, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
src: Rule 50(10) and its Explanation, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Assuming the father takes first

q: A pensioner marries after retirement. He must intimate the change to the Head of Office:
opts: by an ordinary letter; no form is prescribed
in Form 5, with a copy of the marriage certificate
in Format 5, with a copy of the marriage certificate
in Form 4, with a copy of the marriage certificate
expl:
( B) in Form 5, with a copy of the marriage certificate.
(A) by an ordinary letter; no form is prescribed. — Rule 50(15)(f) prescribes Form 5 and the certificate.
(C) in Format 5, with a copy of the marriage certificate. — Format 5 is the relieving order on absorption.
(D) in Form 4, with a copy of the marriage certificate. — Form 4 is the pre-retirement family particulars form, re-submitted with the pension papers.

Rule 50(15)(a) requires the family particulars in Form 4 on entering service, and clause (e) requires an up-to-date Form 4 with the pension papers before retirement. Clause (f) then deals with events after retirement: where the servant marries or remarries, or a child is born, he must intimate the Head of Office in Form 5 with a copy of the marriage or birth certificate, as the case may be.

Exam-safe point: Post-retirement change of family: Form 5, with the certificate.

Statutory Authority: Rule 50(15)(f), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Answering Form 4 for a post-retirement event

q: Where a disability manifests in a child or dependent sibling, the fact must be supported by a medical certificate from:
opts: the Pension Disbursing Authority — The disbursing authority has no certifying role under this clause
an authority competent to issue a disability certificate under the RPwD Act, 2016, or a Medical Board
the Head of Office's own assessment
any registered medical practitioner — Rule 50(15)(c) names two specific sources
expl:
( B) an authority competent to issue a disability certificate under the RPwD Act, 2016, or a Medical Board.
(C) the Head of Office's own assessment. — The Head of Office receives and records the certificate; he does not issue it.

Rule 50(15)(c) requires the fact of a disability to be supported by a certificate from either an authority competent to issue a disability certificate under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and the Rules of 2017, or a Medical Board comprising a Medical Superintendent, Principal, Director or Head of the Institution or his nominee as Chairman and two other members, at least one of whom is a specialist in the particular area of disability.

Exam-safe point: Disability: an RPwD-authorised authority or a Medical Board.

Statutory Authority: Rule 50(15)(c), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Accepting any doctor's certificate

q: A Government servant goes missing and a police report is lodged. Death gratuity becomes payable:
opts: when the death is conclusively established, or on expiry of seven years from the police report, whichever is earlier
on expiry of twelve years from the police report — The period is seven years
on expiry of six months from the police report
only when the death is conclusively established, however long it takes
expl:
( A) when the death is conclusively established, or on expiry of seven years from the police report, whichever is earlier.
(C) on expiry of six months from the police report. — Six months is the waiting period before family pension and gratuity may start, not the trigger.
(D) only when the death is conclusively established, however long it takes. — The seven-year limb exists precisely for the case where death is never established.

Rule 51(8)(a) bars payment of family pension, including arrears, and of gratuity before six months from the date of lodging the police report. Clause (b) then fixes when death gratuity becomes payable: after the death is conclusively established, or on expiry of seven years from the date of the report, whichever is earlier. Clause (c) requires any difference between death gratuity and retirement gratuity to be paid within three months of the claim.

Exam-safe point: Death gratuity: conclusive proof or seven years, whichever is earlier.

Statutory Authority: Rule 51(8), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Applying the six-month wait to the death gratuity trigger

q: A claim in a missing-person case must be accompanied by:
opts: a death certificate from the registering authority
a succession certificate
an indemnity bond in Format 7, with the same reports
an indemnity bond in Format 8, with copies of the police report and the untraced report
expl:
( D) an indemnity bond in Format 8, with copies of the police report and the untraced report.
(A) a death certificate from the registering authority. — Rule 71(6)(e) expressly says the Head of Office shall not wait for one.
(B) a succession certificate. — A succession certificate belongs to the rule 49 route where there is no family.
(C) an indemnity bond in Format 7, with the same reports. — Format 7 is the indemnity bond for a minor's share of gratuity.

Rule 51(5)(a) requires claims to be submitted after a police report has been lodged as an FIR, daily diary entry or general diary entry. Clause (b) requires the claim to be accompanied by an Indemnity Bond in Format 8 together with a copy of that report and a report from the police that the person could not be traced despite all efforts. Rule 71(6)(e) reinforces the scheme by directing the Head of Office not to wait for a death certificate.

Exam-safe point: Missing person: Format 8 indemnity bond plus the two police reports.

Statutory Authority: Rule 51(5) and rule 71(6)(e), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Answering Format 7, or waiting for a death certificate

topic: Dearness relief to a family pensioner
q: A family pensioner takes up employment under a State Government. Dearness relief on the family pension:
opts: is suspended during the employment
is payable only if her pay is at the minimum of the scale
continues to be payable during the employment
is payable only after she retires from that employment
expl:
( C) continues to be payable during the employment.
(A) is suspended during the employment. — That is the rule for a pensioner, not for a family pensioner.
(B) is payable only if her pay is at the minimum of the scale. — The minimum-of-scale condition belongs to rule 52(2), which rule 52(4) disapplies here.
(D) is payable only after she retires from that employment. — Rule 52(4) preserves it during the employment.

Rule 52(2) denies dearness relief to a pensioner or compassionate allowance holder who is re-employed or absorbed, subject to the three-condition proviso in rule 52(2) and the certificate regime in rule 52(3). Rule 52(4) carves family pensioners out of that denial: a family pensioner employed under the Central or State Government or a corporation, company, body or bank under them remains eligible to draw dearness relief on family pension during the employment.

Exam-safe point: Family pensioner employed: dearness relief continues.

Statutory Authority: Rule 52(2) to (4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Applying the re-employment bar to a family pensioner

q: Every Head of Department must prepare a list of servants due to retire within the next fifteen months:
opts: by the 1st day of every month
by the last day of every month
by the 15th day of every month
once a year, in January
expl:
( C) by the 15th day of every month.
(A) by the 1st day of every month. — The rule fixes the fifteenth.
(B) by the last day of every month. — The last day is when a copy goes to the Accounts Officer under rule 54(2).
(D) once a year, in January. — The list is monthly.

Rule 54(1) requires every Head of Department to have a list prepared by the 15th day of every month of all Government servants due to retire within the next fifteen months of that date. Rule 54(2) requires a copy to the Accounts Officer before the last day of every month. Rule 54(3) deals with other retirements: the Head of Office must inform the Accounts Officer within ten days of the order.

Exam-safe point: List by the 15th; copy to Accounts Officer by the month's last day.

Statutory Authority: Rule 54, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Swapping the fifteenth and the last day of the month

q: Preparatory work for processing a pension case begins:
opts: eight months before retirement, when the third stage begins
one year before retirement, or on proceeding on leave preparatory to retirement, whichever is earlier
on the date of the retirement order — That is the rule 58 trigger for other retirements
six months before retirement, when Form 4 and Form 6 fall due
expl:
( B) one year before retirement, or on proceeding on leave preparatory to retirement, whichever is earlier.
(A) eight months before retirement, when the third stage begins. — Eight months is a deadline within the year, not its start.
(D) six months before retirement, when Form 4 and Form 6 fall due. — The six-month point is the deadline for those forms under rule 57(2)(a), not the start of preparation.

Rule 56 requires every Head of Office to undertake the preparatory work one year before the date of superannuation retirement, or on the date the servant proceeds on leave preparatory to retirement, whichever is earlier. Rule 57 divides that year into three stages, with verification of service complete eight months before superannuation and the third stage beginning no later than eight months before retirement.

Exam-safe point: One year out, or on leave preparatory to retirement, whichever is earlier.

Statutory Authority: Rule 56 and rule 57(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Starting at the six-month or eight-month milestone

q: A Head of Office refers a period of service to another office for verification and receives no response within the two months allowed. The period:
opts: is deemed to qualify for pension
is held in abeyance until the other office replies
must be verified from pay bills by the referring office
is treated as non-qualifying
expl:
( A) is deemed to qualify for pension.
(B) is held in abeyance until the other office replies. — The deeming provision exists to prevent that delay.
(C) must be verified from pay bills by the referring office. — That is the sub-clause (ii) route, not the consequence of silence.
(D) is treated as non-qualifying. — The rule deems the opposite where no response comes.

Rule 57(1)(a)(iv) gives the office receiving a verification reference two months to verify and reply, with a proviso requiring any period incapable of verification to be flagged at once. Sub-clause (v) then provides that if no response is received within that time, the period shall be deemed to qualify for pension. Sub-clause (vi) fixes responsibility on the Secretary of the Ministry where a non-qualifying period was not communicated.

Exam-safe point: Silence for two months: the period is deemed to qualify.

Statutory Authority: Rule 57(1)(a)(iv) to (vi), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Treating silence as exclusion

q: For calculating emoluments and average emoluments, the Head of Office verifies correctness of emoluments:
opts: for the entire service
for the last ten months only
for the whole of the last five years — The rule expressly stops at twenty-four months
only for the twenty-four months preceding retirement, and no earlier period
expl:
( D) only for the twenty-four months preceding retirement, and no earlier period.
(A) for the entire service. — The rule expressly confines verification to twenty-four months.
(B) for the last ten months only. — Ten months is the averaging window; the verification window is twenty-four.

Rule 57(1)(b)(iv) requires the Head of Office to verify from the service book the correctness of the emoluments drawn or to be drawn during the last ten months of service. Sub-clause (v) then limits that exercise: to ensure those ten months are correctly shown, the Head of Office verifies correctness only for the twenty-four months preceding retirement, and not for any period before that date. Rule 63(1)(c) imposes the same limit on the Accounts Officer.

Exam-safe point: Twenty-four months, not the ten-month averaging window.

Statutory Authority: Rule 57(1)(b)(v) and rule 63(1)(c), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Equating the ten-month average with the verification window

q: Where provisional pension and gratuity are sanctioned under rule 62, the sanction authorises:
opts: two-thirds of pension, and the full gratuity
100 per cent of pension, but no gratuity at all
50 per cent of pension and 90 per cent of gratuity — Neither figure appears in rule 62(3)
100 per cent of pension, and 100 per cent of gratuity withholding ten per cent of the gratuity
expl:
( D) 100 per cent of pension, and 100 per cent of gratuity withholding ten per cent of the gratuity.
(A) two-thirds of pension, and the full gratuity. — Two-thirds is the rule 40 provisional figure for compulsory retirement.
(B) 100 per cent of pension, but no gratuity at all. — That is the position under rule 8 where proceedings are pending.

Rule 62(3)(a) requires the Head of Office to authorise, from the date following retirement, 100 per cent of pension as provisional pension and 100 per cent of the gratuity as provisional gratuity while withholding ten per cent of the gratuity. Rule 62(4) requires the sanction within ten days after retirement on superannuation, or within one month of the forms for other retirements, and rule 62(6)(a) caps provisional pension at six months.

Exam-safe point: 100 per cent of both, with ten per cent of gratuity withheld.

Statutory Authority: Rule 62(3) to (6), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Importing the rule 40 two-thirds figure

q: The final pension and gratuity are not determined within six months of the provisional sanction. The Accounts Officer:
opts: shall refer the case to the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare
shall continue the provisional pension indefinitely — Rule 62(7) converts it instead of extending it
shall treat the provisional pension and gratuity as final and issue the PPO on expiry of the six months
shall recover the provisional pension paid — The rule converts the provisional payment; it does not recover it
expl:
( C) shall treat the provisional pension and gratuity as final and issue the PPO on expiry of the six months.
(A) shall refer the case to the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare. — No such reference is provided for in rule 62(7).

Rule 62(6)(a) caps provisional pension at six months from retirement or from submission of Form 4 and Form 6, whichever is later. Rule 62(7) then provides that where the final amounts have not been determined within that period, the Accounts Officer shall treat the provisional pension and gratuity as final and issue the pension payment order immediately on the expiry of the six months. Rule 62(8) then releases the withheld gratuity.

Exam-safe point: Six months: provisional becomes final.

Statutory Authority: Rule 62(6) to (8), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Reading the six months as extendable

q: The Accounts Officer must issue the pension payment order for a superannuation retirement:
opts: on the date of retirement itself
not later than two months before the date of retirement
within forty five days of receiving the papers
within one month of receiving the papers
expl:
( B) not later than two months before the date of retirement.
(A) on the date of retirement itself. — The rule requires issue in advance of that date.
(C) within forty five days of receiving the papers. — The forty-five-day limit applies to retirements other than on superannuation under clause (b).
(D) within one month of receiving the papers. — One month is the family pension timeline under rule 76(1), not this one.

Rule 63(1)(a) requires the Accounts Officer, on receiving the pension case under rule 60, to apply the checks, record the enfacement in Part II of Form 7, assess pension, family pension and gratuity, and issue the pension payment order not later than two months before the date of superannuation retirement. Clause (b) gives forty-five days from receipt of the papers where the retirement is otherwise than on superannuation.

Exam-safe point: Two months in advance for superannuation; forty-five days otherwise.

Statutory Authority: Rule 63(1)(a) and (b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Using the forty-five-day limit for a superannuation case

q: A servant retires on superannuation and his pension is paid late for administrative reasons. Interest runs from:
opts: the date following the expiry of three months from the date of retirement
the date of retirement itself
the date six months after retirement
the date following the expiry of one month from retirement
expl:
( A) the date following the expiry of three months from the date of retirement.
(B) the date of retirement itself. — Interest begins only after the three-month grace period.
(C) the date six months after retirement. — Six months is the missing-person waiting period, not the interest trigger.
(D) the date following the expiry of one month from retirement. — The period is three months.

Rule 65(1) allows interest on arrears at the rate applicable to General Provident Fund amounts where delay is attributable to administrative reasons or lapses, unless the delay was the servant's own failure to comply with the procedure. Rule 65(5)(a) then fixes the start of the period for a superannuation retirement at the date following the expiry of three months from retirement, running to the date of payment.

Exam-safe point: Interest: three months after retirement.

Statutory Authority: Rule 65(1) and (5)(a), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Starting interest from the date of retirement

topic: Revision to the disadvantage of a pensioner
q: A clerical error in a pension authorised two years and three months ago is detected. The pension may be revised to the pensioner's disadvantage:
opts: only with the concurrence of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare
never, because more than two years have passed
only with the sanction of the Ministry of Finance
on the Head of Office's own authority
expl:
( A) only with the concurrence of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare.
(B) never, because more than two years have passed. — The rule permits revision with concurrence; it does not bar it.
(C) only with the sanction of the Ministry of Finance. — The Ministry of Finance is consulted under rule 66(4) on waiver of recovery, not on the revision.
(D) on the Head of Office's own authority. — The proviso requires a higher concurrence after two years.

Rule 66(2) protects a pension once authorised, permitting revision to the disadvantage of the pensioner only where a clerical error is subsequently detected. Its proviso adds that where the error is detected more than two years after authorisation or revision, no such revision may be ordered without the concurrence of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare. Rule 66(3) leaves the question whether an error is clerical to the administrative Ministry.

Exam-safe point: After two years: DP&PW concurrence.

Statutory Authority: Rule 66(2) and its proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
src: Rule 66(2) and its proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Treating the two-year point as an absolute bar

q: Which of these may NOT be recovered from retirement gratuity?
opts: Arrears of income tax deductible at source
Balance of a house building advance
Arrears of licence fee for Government accommodation
A personal loan taken by the servant from a cooperative society
expl:
( D) A personal loan taken by the servant from a cooperative society.
(A) Arrears of income tax deductible at source. — Clause (b) names it expressly.
(B) Balance of a house building advance. — A house building advance is Government dues under clause (b).
(C) Arrears of licence fee for Government accommodation. — Clause (a) covers accommodation dues and related charges.

Rule 67(2) adjusts against retirement gratuity the Government dues assessed by the Head of Office and outstanding at retirement. The Explanation defines Government dues as accommodation dues including licence fee arrears, damages, and electricity, water and PNG charges under clause (a), and under clause (b) the balance of house building, conveyance or other advances, overpayment of pay, allowances or leave salary, and arrears of income tax deductible at source. Rule 67(3) then forbids recovery of anything that is not Government dues in that sense.

Exam-safe point: Only Government dues come out of gratuity.

Statutory Authority: Rule 67(2) and (3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Recovering a private debt from gratuity

q: The Directorate of Estates must issue a No Demand Certificate after the accommodation is vacated:
opts: within seven days of the application
within one month of the application
within fourteen days of the application
within two months of the application
expl:
( C) within fourteen days of the application.
(A) within seven days of the application. — Seven days is the rule 71(4)(c) period for a death intimation.
(B) within one month of the application. — The period is fourteen days.
(D) within two months of the application. — Two months is the period for the Directorate's reply under rule 68(1)(a).

Rule 68(7)(a) requires the Directorate of Estates to give the No Demand Certificate within fourteen days of the application made after actual vacation of the accommodation. Clause (b) entitles the allottee to interest at General Provident Fund rates on the excess withheld gratuity if the certificate is delayed beyond that, and clause (c) makes the Directorate of Estates pay it through the Accounts Officer.

Exam-safe point: Fourteen days for the No Demand Certificate.

Statutory Authority: Rule 68(7), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Using the two-month or one-month periods from rule 68(1)

q: The office fails to issue the retirement notification on time. The servant:
opts: continues in service until the notification issues — Rule 70(2) expressly denies that consequence
is deemed to have retired on attaining the age of superannuation, and is not entitled to continue
must apply afresh for pension — Pension follows from the deemed retirement
is entitled to pay for the period of delay
expl:
( B) is deemed to have retired on attaining the age of superannuation, and is not entitled to continue.
(D) is entitled to pay for the period of delay. — The rule does not create a right to pay for a failure to notify.

Rule 70(1) requires a Gazette notification for a Gazetted servant, or an office order for a non-Gazetted servant, specifying the date of retirement within a week, with a copy to the Accounts Officer. Rule 70(2) then provides that unless specific extension orders issue, the servant is deemed to have retired on attaining the age of superannuation, and the office's failure to issue the notification does not entitle him to continue beyond that date.

Exam-safe point: Deemed retirement on the superannuation date, notification or not.

Statutory Authority: Rule 70, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Treating the notification as constitutive of retirement

q: A Government servant dies while in occupation of Government accommodation. The licence fee outstanding for the period before his death:
opts: is recovered from the provident fund
stands waived
is recovered from the family pension
is recovered from the death gratuity
expl:
( B) stands waived.
(A) is recovered from the provident fund. — The rule provides no such recovery.
(C) is recovered from the family pension. — The rule waives the pre-death licence fee.
(D) is recovered from the death gratuity. — Only dues relating to damages are recovered from death gratuity.

Rule 71(4)(a) waives the dues pertaining to outstanding licence fee for the period before the date of death of a servant who was an allottee. Clause (b) keeps dues relating to damages recoverable from the death gratuity, and provides that if the family retains the accommodation, no licence fee is recovered for the month of death and the first three months after it. Clause (c) requires the Head of Office to write to the Directorate of Estates within seven days.

Exam-safe point: Pre-death licence fee waived; damages still recoverable.

Statutory Authority: Rule 71(4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Recovering the waived licence fee from death gratuity

q: On death of a servant in service, provisional family pension must be drawn:
opts: within fifteen days of receipt of the claim
within forty five days of receipt of the claim
within seven days of receipt of the claim
within one month of receipt of the claim
expl:
( A) within fifteen days of receipt of the claim.
(B) within forty five days of receipt of the claim. — Forty-five days is the invalid pension period under rule 39(8).
(C) within seven days of receipt of the claim. — Seven days is the intimation period to the Directorate of Estates.
(D) within one month of receipt of the claim. — One month is the rule 74(1) period for forwarding the case, and the rule 76(1) period for the Accounts Officer.

Rule 75(1) requires the Head of Office, once satisfied of the claimant's eligibility, to draw provisional family pension not exceeding the maximum admissible, within fifteen days of receipt of the claim, issuing a sanction letter and drawing the amount as establishment pay is drawn. Rule 75(3) continues it for six months from the day after death unless extended under rule 76.

Exam-safe point: Provisional family pension: fifteen days.

Statutory Authority: Rule 75(1) and (3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Using the one-month case-forwarding period

q: The maximum amount of gratuity that may be held over pending assessment of Government dues on a death case is:
opts: one-third of the amount of gratuity
fifty per cent of the amount of gratuity
twenty per cent of the amount of gratuity
ten per cent of the amount of gratuity
expl:
( D) ten per cent of the amount of gratuity.
(A) one-third of the amount of gratuity. — One-third is the rule 8(6) recovery cap.
(B) fifty per cent of the amount of gratuity. — No such figure appears in rule 74.
(C) twenty per cent of the amount of gratuity. — Twenty per cent is the rule 47(7) minor's-share figure.

Rule 74(4) requires the Head of Office to draw the Accounts Officer's attention to outstanding Government dues, including under clause (b) the amount of gratuity held over partly for adjustment of unassessed dues and partly as a margin, and clause (c) caps that held-over amount at ten per cent of the gratuity. Rule 76(5)(e) then provides for adjustment of the withheld amount against outstanding licence fee and refund of the balance.

Exam-safe point: Held-over gratuity: ten per cent maximum.

Statutory Authority: Rule 74(4) and rule 76(5)(e), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Confusing it with the one-third recovery cap

topic: Sanction of family pension on a pensioner's death
q: A pensioner dies leaving a family member not named in the pension payment order. The Head of Office sanctions family pension:
opts: in Format 12, within one month of the claim
in Form 13, within one month of the claim
in Format 13, within one month of receipt of the claim in Form 10
in Form 10, within three months of the claim
expl:
( C) in Format 13, within one month of receipt of the claim in Form 10.
(A) in Format 12, within one month of the claim. — Format 12 is the letter inviting the claim, not the sanction.
(B) in Form 13, within one month of the claim. — Form 13 is the residuary gratuity claim.
(D) in Form 10, within three months of the claim. — Form 10 is the claim itself, and the period is one month.

Rule 79(2)(b)(i) applies where the pension payment order names no family member, or where the person now entitled is someone else, including a person who joined the family after retirement. The Head of Office must, within one month of receiving a claim in Form 10, sanction the family pension in Format 13 in favour of the person entitled. Rule 80(1) then requires the Accounts Officer to authorise payment within one month of the sanction.

Exam-safe point: Sanction: Format 13, on a Form 10 claim, within one month.

Statutory Authority: Rule 79(2)(b)(i) and rule 80(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Answering Format 12 or Form 13

q: A claim for residuary gratuity on the death of a retired servant is made in:
opts: Form 9
Format 13
Form 13
Form 12
expl:
( C) Form 13.
(A) Form 9. — Form 9 is the death gratuity claim by a nominee or family member.
(B) Format 13. — Format 13 is the Head of Office's sanction of family pension.
(D) Form 12. — Form 12 is the family pension claim against a pensioner's PPO.

Rule 79(6) provides that where a residuary gratuity becomes payable to the family of a deceased retired servant under rule 45(3), the Head of Office sanctions its payment on receipt of a claim in Form 13 from the person or persons eligible. Rule 45(3) grants the residuary gratuity where the sums received by the pensioner before death fall short of twelve times his emoluments within five years of retirement.

Exam-safe point: Residuary gratuity: claim in Form 13.

Statutory Authority: Rule 79(6) and rule 45(3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Answering Format 13 for the claim

topic: Pension for the day of death
q: Pension, including family pension, is payable:
opts: only up to the last working day of the month
for the day on which its recipient dies
for the whole month in which the recipient dies
up to the day before the recipient dies
expl:
( B) for the day on which its recipient dies.
(A) only up to the last working day of the month. — That is the payment convention in rule 83(2), not the accrual.
(C) for the whole month in which the recipient dies. — The rule fixes the day of death, not the whole month.
(D) up to the day before the recipient dies. — Rule 81(3) includes the day of death.

Rule 81(1) makes pension other than family pension payable from the date the servant ceases to be borne on the establishment. Rule 81(2) makes family pension payable from the day after the death or ineligibility, subject to rule 76(2)(d) and rule 79(3)(iv). Rule 81(3) then provides that pension, including family pension, is payable for the day on which its recipient dies.

Exam-safe point: The day of death is a pension day.

Statutory Authority: Rule 81, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Stopping pension on the day before death

q: A monthly pension is payable:
opts: on or after the last working day of the month to which it relates, except March
on the first working day of every month without exception
in advance, on the first day of the month to which it relates
on the last working day of every month without exception — March is the exception
expl:
( A) on or after the last working day of the month to which it relates, except March.
(B) on the first working day of every month without exception. — Only March is paid on or after the first working day of April.
(C) in advance, on the first day of the month to which it relates. — Payment is on or after the last working day, not in advance.

Rule 83(1) requires gratuity to be paid in lump sum. Rule 83(2) makes a pension fixed at monthly rates payable monthly on or after the last working day of the month to which it relates, except for the month of March, when it is payable on or after the first working day of April. Rule 82 confines all pensions and gratuities to rupees in India.

Exam-safe point: Last working day, with March paid in April.

Statutory Authority: Rules 82 and 83, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Forgetting the March exception

q: A doubt arises on the interpretation of the pension rules. It is referred to:
opts: the Central Administrative Tribunal — The Tribunal adjudicates disputes; it is not the interpretative authority
the Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure) in every case — The Ministry of Finance is consulted on waiver of recovery under rule 66(4)
the Comptroller and Auditor General — The C&AG audits; it does not decide interpretation
the Government in the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare or the Department of Personnel and Training, depending on the rule or subject
expl:
( D) the Government in the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare or the Department of Personnel and Training, depending on the rule or subject.

Rule 85 requires a doubt on the interpretation of the rules to be referred for decision to the Government in the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare or the Department of Personnel and Training, depending on the rule or the subject on which a decision is required and the Department concerned with it. Rule 86 separately allows a Ministry to relax a rule causing undue hardship, with the concurrence of one of those two Departments.

Exam-safe point: Interpretation: DP&PW or DoPT, by subject.

Statutory Authority: Rules 85 and 86, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Sending every question to the Ministry of Finance

q: A Ministry wishes to relax a rule that is causing undue hardship. It may do so:
opts: only with the approval of the President
on its own authority, recording reasons
only through a fresh notification amending the rules
by order recording reasons, with the concurrence of DP&PW or DoPT
expl:
( D) by order recording reasons, with the concurrence of DP&PW or DoPT.
(A) only with the approval of the President. — The concurrence required is departmental, not presidential.
(B) on its own authority, recording reasons. — The proviso requires the concurrence of one of the two Departments.
(C) only through a fresh notification amending the rules. — Rule 86 is a relaxation power, not an amendment route.

Rule 86 permits a Ministry or Department satisfied that a rule causes undue hardship to dispense with or relax it by order for reasons recorded in writing, to the extent and on the exceptions and conditions it considers just and equitable. The proviso forbids any such order except with the concurrence of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare or the Department of Personnel and Training, according to the rule or subject.

Exam-safe point: Relaxation: reasoned order plus DP&PW or DoPT concurrence.

Statutory Authority: Rule 86 and its proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
src: Rule 86 and its proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Relaxing a rule without concurrence

q: A pension case of a servant who retired before the 2021 Rules commenced is pending on commencement. It is decided:
opts: under the 2021 Rules, because they are now in force
by the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare
under the old rules, as if the 2021 Rules had not been made
under whichever set of rules is more beneficial
expl:
( C) under the old rules, as if the 2021 Rules had not been made.
(A) under the 2021 Rules, because they are now in force. — Rule 87(2)(c) saves the old law for pending cases.
(B) by the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare. — The saving prescribes the law, not a new authority.
(D) under whichever set of rules is more beneficial. — The saving is not a beneficial-choice provision.

Rule 87(1) repeals the old rules, including the CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972, so far as they provide for matters now contained in the 2021 Rules. Rule 87(2) saves nominations, family particulars and pension applications made under the old rules, and requires pending cases of authorisation of pension under clause (c), and of gratuity and family pension under clause (d), to be disposed of under the old rules as if the new rules had not been made.

Exam-safe point: Pending cases: the old rules still govern.

Statutory Authority: Rule 87, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Applying the new rules to a case pending on commencement

q: A nomination for gratuity made under the 1972 Rules before commencement of the 2021 Rules:
opts: lapses on commencement and must be re-made
is deemed to have been made under the corresponding provisions of the 2021 Rules
continues under the 1972 Rules indefinitely — It is deemed to be made under the new rules
must be re-executed in Form 3 within six months
expl:
( B) is deemed to have been made under the corresponding provisions of the 2021 Rules.
(A) lapses on commencement and must be re-made. — Rule 87(2)(a)(i) saves it rather than letting it lapse.
(D) must be re-executed in Form 3 within six months. — No re-execution period is imposed on a saved nomination.

Rule 87(2)(a) treats every nomination for gratuity, every form giving family details for family pension, and every formal application for sanction of pension made under the old rules as made under the corresponding provisions of the 2021 Rules. Clause (b) deals with the opposite case, requiring a nomination or family form not yet made to be made under the new rules after commencement.

Exam-safe point: Old nominations carry over as if made under the new rules.

Statutory Authority: Rule 87(2)(a) and (b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
trap: Treating saved nominations as lapsed
